Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i've got scans of the geology field notebook from the ridge traverse, and i need to sort out sample locations. before doing that, check whether there's a visible north arrow on every scanned page. the arrows matter because i only want the location entries extracted when all the pages have that reference. if every page has a visible north arrow, put the sample-location entries in a table, one entry per row, with the page number, sample ID, and location as written. keep the coordinates and wording as they appear, and don't guess at anything illegible. if even one page doesn't have a visible north arrow, don't extract any of the sample locations; instead, give me the page numbers where an arrow is missing. no need to list pages that have one. use the scans, not outside sources, and if a page number itself can't be read, don't infer it. i just need the table if all pages pass the check, or the missing-arrow page list otherwise. output only that result, no introduction or explanation.", "output": "Check the scanned geology field notebook pages from the ridge traverse for a visible north arrow on every page.

- If every page has a visible north arrow, extract the sample-location entries into a table with one entry per row and these columns: page number, sample ID, and location as written. Keep the coordinates and wording as they appear. Do not guess at illegible information.
- If any page is missing a visible north arrow, do not extract the sample locations. Instead, list only the page numbers where an arrow is missing; do not list pages that have one.

Use only the scans. Do not infer an unreadable page number. Output only the table if every page passes the check, or the missing-arrow page list otherwise, with no introduction or explanation."}]
